bear.writtenAnchor: Membership warehouse growth slows toward the weakest year in the filed window: traffic normalises, new-club openings and comparable sales decelerate, and revenue compounds near the 5.0% low end of the single-year range in H:revenue. Price investment and wage pressure push operating margin back toward the filed middle/low of the 3.1%-3.9% band in H:margin, so profit grows slower than revenue. New capital still earns a decent but much lower return than the 48.3% incremental figure in H:returns, and modest net share creep from stock-based compensation (H:cashflow) dilutes per-share outcomes. Capital spending keeps rising (H:capex) but buys less growth.

revenueGrowthOrPath.text: The weakest single year in the filed window was 5.0% growth (H:revenue); the bear case assumes that trough rate persists for five years rather than the 10.0% nine-year CAGR.

operatingMargin.text: Operating margin has ranged 3.1% to 3.9% over ten years with a 3.4% median (H:margin); the bear case gives back most of the recent expansion and settles just below the median, still inside the filed band.

reinvestmentCapitalIntensity.text: Net investment at the filed median of capex minus D&A over revenue, 0.9%, which is what a slower-opening Costco would spend (H:capex).

returnOnNewInvestment.text: New warehouses earn far less than the installed base: 15% is well under every filed annual ROIC (27.9% to 41.8%) and under the 48.3% five-year incremental return, and it is allowed to sit above the 9.0% discount rate but below the base case's terminal return (H:returns).

shareCount.text: Stock-based compensation has risen every filed year to 924m in FY2026 (H:cashflow); if repurchase activity is cut back in a weaker environment, net issuance leaves the diluted count modestly higher over five years. (1.02× today's diluted count)

base.writtenAnchor: Costco keeps compounding at roughly its recent pace: FY2026 revenue of 303154m was up about 10% on FY2025 and the latest quarter grew 11.1% (H:revenue, H:quarter), so a high-single-digit constant rate for years 1-5 sits inside the filed range with room to spare. Operating margin holds near the FY2026 level of 3.9%, the top of the ten-year filed band but the end point of a steady upward drift from 3.1% (H:margin), supported by membership fee income and scale. Net reinvestment stays a little above the 0.9% median as capex outruns D&A (H:capex), and new capital earns a return well below the 48.3% recent incremental figure but comfortably above the terminal hurdle (H:returns). Share count is roughly flat as buyback and settlement activity offsets SBC (H:cashflow).

revenueGrowthOrPath.text: FY2026 revenue of 303154m was about 10% above FY2025 and the latest quarter grew 11.1% year on year (H:revenue, H:quarter); 8% is set below the recent run-rate and below the 10.0% window CAGR to allow for normal deceleration, and sits inside the 5.0%-17.5% filed range.

operatingMargin.text: FY2026 operating margin was 3.9%, the top of the filed range and the end point of a steady rise from 3.1% in FY2019 (H:margin); the base case holds the current level rather than extrapolating further gains.

reinvestmentCapitalIntensity.text: FY2026 capex of 6435m less D&A of 2674m is 3761m, about 1.2% of the 303154m revenue, above the 0.9% ten-year median as the build programme has stepped up (H:capex, H:revenue).

returnOnNewInvestment.text: FY2026 ROIC was 41.8% and five-year incremental return on new capital was 48.3% (H:returns); 35% is below both and below the 1.5x cap on the best filed return, and sits above the base terminal return of 12.0% (9.0% discount rate plus the wide-moat credit).

shareCount.text: SBC of 924m in FY2026 against operating cash flow of 15817m is small (H:cashflow); the base case assumes repurchases roughly offset issuance and the diluted count is unchanged. (1× today's diluted count)

bull.writtenAnchor: Warehouse openings accelerate internationally and e-commerce plus ancillary businesses lift throughput, so revenue grows near the upper half of the filed single-year range (H:revenue) with the 11.1% latest quarter (H:quarter) as the running start. Operating margin extends the decade-long climb from 3.1% to 3.9% a little further as membership fees and scale leverage fixed cost (H:margin). New capital continues to earn close to the 48.3% five-year incremental return in H:returns, so even a higher reinvestment share out of the rising capex line (H:capex) converts into compounding profit, and a slightly shrinking share count (H:cashflow) concentrates the result.

revenueGrowthOrPath.text: The latest quarter grew 11.1% and the filed single-year range reaches 17.5% (H:quarter, H:revenue); holding roughly the current reported pace for five years is the optimistic but filed-supported case.

operatingMargin.text: Margin improved every year from 3.3% in FY2023 to 3.9% in FY2026 (H:margin); the bull extends that trend modestly to 4.3%, within the allowed five points above the filed high.

reinvestmentCapitalIntensity.text: Faster growth needs more warehouses: net investment at 1.4% of revenue, modestly above the FY2026 rate of about 1.2% (capex 6435m less D&A 2674m on 303154m) and the 0.9% median (H:capex, H:revenue).

returnOnNewInvestment.text: New capital over the last five filed years earned 48.3% incrementally and FY2026 ROIC was 41.8% (H:returns); the bull case assumes new clubs keep earning close to that, still under the 1.5x cap, and above the bull terminal return of 13.5%.

shareCount.text: Operating cash flow grew from 11068m in FY2023 to 15817m in FY2026 while SBC rose only from 774m to 924m (H:cashflow); surplus cash funds a small net reduction in shares. (0.98× today's diluted count)

moatAnchor.text: Cost advantage and efficient scale: purchasing and distribution scale on 303154m of FY2026 revenue let the company sell at thin gross margins, which shows up as a consistently high return on capital rather than a high margin. Filed ROIC never fell below 27.9% in ten years and reached 41.8% in FY2026, with recent incremental return on new capital of 48.3% (H:returns); the 3.1%-3.9% operating margin band is deliberately thin yet the capital turn is high enough to keep returns far above the 9.0% discount rate, and a 12.0% terminal return is well below every filed year.

constantsAnchor.text: No company tax-rate disclosure was supplied, so the general US federal statutory rate of 21.0% is used, which is also the rate on which the filed NOPAT and ROIC series rests (STATUTORY, H:returns). The stress margin of 3.1% is the lowest operating margin in the ten filed years (FY2019) and is below both the 3.9% current and 3.4% median margins (H:margin).

provisionalLabels.preRevenueConstructionLeadYears: First-order estimate; worth $27/share on OKLO's 8 GW case (§7.1).
provisionalLabels.leveredCostOfEquityCap: No observations behind the 30% level itself; capped cells are labelled RATE CAPPED — VALUE IS AN UPPER BOUND (I12, §7.1).
provisionalLabels.gate0InterestIncomeOverRevenueThreshold: No observations behind it (Appendix B); the other three Gate 0 tests are classification lookups, not thresholds (§6.1).
provisionalLabels.gate1HistoryInsufficientYears: Red-team judgment with no observations (Appendix B). Direction of error is suppression, so a wrong threshold shows less rather than something false (§6.2).
provisionalLabels.gate1ShortHistoryYears: Red-team judgment with no observations (Appendix B), same basis as the <5-year threshold (§6.2).
provisionalLabels.historyInsufficientStressMarginRelativeR: No observations; substitutes for a median that does not exist under HISTORY INSUFFICIENT (§6.2).
provisionalLabels.runRateSequentialGrowthTrigger: Calibrated on NVIDIA only (Appendix B) (§7.2 M12).
provisionalLabels.seasonalityPriorYearThreshold: Comes from I4 and has no observations behind it (§7.2 M12).
